THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Friendsgiving Green Bean Chicken Casserole

Green bean casserole, but make it dinner. My kids couldn’t tell there was cottage cheese in the sauce, and I bet your guests won’t either.

YIELD8 servings
TOTAL TIME35 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~360 cal | ~34g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Blend the 16 oz Nancy’s 2% cottage cheese and 1/2 cup Nurri whole protein milk until completely smooth before starting the pan.

Ingredients

Shared

  • 30 oz Del Real pulled chicken (two 15 oz packs)
  • 16 oz green beans, trimmed/chopped
  • 8 oz sliced mushrooms + 1 medium diced onion + 4 minced garlic cloves
  • 1/2 tbsp avocado oil + 4 tbsp all-purpose flour + 1 cup Kirkland chicken bone broth
  • 16 oz Nancy’s 2% cottage cheese + 1/2 cup Nurri whole protein milk
  • 8 oz Velveeta Mexican shreds + 1/2 tsp dried thyme + 1/4 tsp rubbed sage + 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • 4 oz Fresh Gourmet crispy onions

Adult Plate — 1/8 Casserole + 1/3 Roasted Sweet Potato Batch (~510 cal / 37g protein)

  • 16 oz pre-cut sweet potatoes (divided across 3 adults)
  • 1/2 tbsp avocado oil + seasoning

Kid Plate — Casserole + Buttered Brioche Rolls

  • Brioche rolls (toasted and buttered; portions not weighed)

You want a cozy holiday or Friendsgiving casserole that eats like comfort food but packs ~34g protein per 1/8 pan (~360 cal), with roasted sweet potatoes for adults (~510 cal, 37g protein plate) and brioche rolls for kids.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.Blend cottage cheese and milk smooth. Blanch green beans until bright green and crisp-tender; drain well.
  2. 2.Heat 1/2 tbsp avocado oil and brown mushrooms and onion until moisture cooks off. Add garlic, thyme, sage, and pepper. Stir in flour and cook briefly, then add bone broth and stir until thickened.
  3. 3.Stir in the blended cottage-cheese sauce, pulled chicken, green beans, and part of the Velveeta shreds. Transfer to a 9×13 dish, top with remaining shreds, and bake at 450°F for 15 minutes until bubbling. Top with crispy onions after baking and rest before serving.

Adult Plate — 1/8 Casserole + 1/3 Roasted Sweet Potato Batch (~510 cal / 37g protein)

  1. 4.Toss 16 oz pre-cut sweet potatoes with 1/2 tbsp avocado oil and seasoning, and roast until tender and browned.
  2. 5.Plate 1/8 of the finished green bean chicken casserole (~360 cal, 34g protein) alongside 1/3 of the roasted sweet potato batch (~150 cal, 2.4g protein) for an ~510 cal, 37g protein dinner plate.

Kid Plate — Casserole + Buttered Brioche Rolls · Kid Plate — Casserole + Buttered Brioche Rolls

  1. 4.Serve a kid portion of the creamy green bean chicken casserole alongside toasted, buttered brioche rolls (kid portions were not weighed, so no child-plate macro is claimed).

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult Plate — 1/8 Casserole + 1/3 Roasted Sweet Potato Batch (~510 cal / 37g protein): Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid Plate — Casserole + Buttered Brioche Rolls: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • Blanch the trimmed, chopped green beans until bright green and crisp-tender, then drain thoroughly so excess water does not thin the sauce.
  • Brown the sliced mushrooms and diced onion in 1/2 tbsp avocado oil until their moisture cooks off, then add garlic, thyme, sage, pepper, flour, and bone broth.

If something fails

Casserole sauce turns watery after baking: Drain the blanched green beans thoroughly and cook the mushrooms and onions until their released moisture evaporates before stirring in the flour and bone broth.

Crispy onions burn or soften in the oven: Bake the casserole with the Velveeta shreds first at 450°F for 15 minutes, then scatter the Fresh Gourmet crispy onions over the bubbling top right after pulling it from the oven.

Storage and reheating

Store: Store leftover casserole in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.

Reheat: Reheat portions in a 375°F oven or air fryer for 8–10 minutes so the crispy onion topping re-crisps.

Lasts: Up to 4 days refrigerated.

Estimated nutrition

~360 cal | ~34g protein.

Whole 9×13 casserole batch (8 servings): ~2,870.5 cal / 275.8g protein / 186.6g carbs / 121.7g fat (~358.8 cal and 34.5g protein per 1/8 pan, displayed as ≈360 cal / 34g protein). Anchored on 30 oz Del Real Pulled Chicken (840 cal, 138g protein), 454g Nancy’s 2% cottage cheese (~330.2 cal, 57.8g protein), 1/2 cup Nurri whole protein milk (85 cal, 10g protein), 8 oz Velveeta Mexican shreds (480 cal, 40g protein), 4 oz Fresh Gourmet crispy onions (648 cal, 0g label protein), 1 cup Kirkland chicken bone broth (45 cal, 9g protein), 1/2 tbsp avocado oil (60 cal), 4 tbsp flour (~109.2 cal, 3.1g protein), 16 oz green beans (~140.6 cal, 8.3g protein), 8 oz mushrooms (~49.9 cal, 7.0g protein), 150g onion (60 cal, 1.7g protein), 12g garlic (~17.9 cal, 0.8g protein), and herbs (~4.7 cal). Adult plate adds 1/3 of a 16 oz raw sweet-potato batch roasted with 1/2 tbsp avocado oil (~150.0 cal, 2.4g protein) for ~508.8 cal and 36.8g protein (displayed as ≈510 cal / 37g protein). Kid brioche plate portions were not weighed.
